title: Graph Plotting Instructions
content:
1. Take 'Number of Rings' on the X-axis and 'D² (cm²)' on the Y-axis.

2. Choose a scale so the plotted points occupy most of the graph sheet — for example, 1 large square = 2 rings on the X-axis, and 1 large square = 0.05 cm² on the Y-axis, adjusted to fit your actual data range.

3. Plot all five (ring number, D²) points and draw the best-fit straight line through them. The line does not need to pass through the origin — a nonzero intercept simply reflects imperfect point contact between the lens and plate, and does not affect the final wavelength calculation.

4. Choose two points that are well separated on the best-fit line itself (not two raw data points) to calculate the slope:
slope = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1)

5. Use this slope in λ2 = slope / (4R) to obtain the graphical estimate of wavelength.

A good graph should show all points lying close to a single straight line. Noticeable scatter usually indicates a reading error somewhere in Table 1.1, while a clean line with an unusual slope usually points to an incorrect value of R.
